newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere gets Paribas export credit up to $110-mln.
newsitem.headline: Solidere gets Paribas export credit up to $110-mln.

text.p: Banque Paribas is heading a syndicate of banks that has granted an export credit of up to $110 million for 10 years to Lebanon's biggest company Solidere, a Paribas executive said on Friday.

Nicolas Constantinesco, Paribas General Manager in Lebanon, said the funds would be paid by Paribas on behalf of Solidere to France's Bouygues and Bouygues Offshore in part payment for building sea defences for the Beirut Central District that Solidere is developing.
"The money is to finance part of the sea defences project which Solidere has contracted to Bouygues and Bouygues Offshore for $230 million," Constantinesco told Reuters.
He said the export credit would be in the $105-$108 million range or "possibly up to $110 million". The interest rate would be about 7.5 percent per annum, he added.
"The combination of the 10-year duration and the interest rate are particularly favourable terms for a Lebanese corporate," Constantinesco said.
He said the syndicate includes Banque Indosuez and the deal would probably be finalised before the end of the year.
"Traditional export financing principles apply to it... The cash does not go to Solidere but is paid by us directly to Bouygues and Bouygues Offshore on behalf of Solidere."

Solidere and the two French firms signed the contract in June. Works, expected to last 30 months, will extend 1,000 metres (yards) around a 150-acre (60-hectare) landfill off the Beirut Central District.
A marina will be built at each end of the sea defences, which will form a double line of defence with a row of massive submerged concrete caissons, a lagoon and a series of quays and promenades.
